def test_solution():
    # Basic case: odd numbers at even indices
    assert solution([1, 2, 3]) == 4  # 1 (idx 0) + 3 (idx 2)
    assert solution([1, 5, 3]) == 4
    assert solution([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) == 9  # 5 (idx 0) + 3 (idx 2) + 1 (idx 4)

    # No odd numbers at even indices
    assert solution([2, 1, 4, 3, 6]) == 0
    assert solution([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == 0

    # All even numbers
    assert solution([2, 4, 6, 8]) == 0

    # All odd numbers
    assert solution([1, 1, 1, 1]) == 2  # idx 0 and idx 2
    assert solution([3, 3, 3, 3, 3]) == 9  # idx 0, 2, 4

    # Empty list
    assert solution([]) == 0

    # Single element: odd
    assert solution([7]) == 7

    # Single element: even
    assert solution([4]) == 0

    # Odd numbers only at odd indices should not count
    assert solution([2, 3, 2, 5, 2]) == 0

    # Negative numbers: -1 % 2 == 1 in Python, so negatives count as odd
    assert solution([-1, 2, -3]) == -4
    assert solution([-2, -1, -4, -3]) == 0  # odd values at odd indices only

    # Larger mixed list
    assert solution([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) == 16  # 1 + 3 + 5 + 7

    # Zero in list
    assert solution([0, 0, 0]) == 0

    # Duplicates
    assert solution([9, 9, 9]) == 18  # idx 0 and 2

    print("All test_solution tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_solution()

import pytest


def test_solution():
    # Basic cases: odd values at even indices
    assert solution([5, 8, 6, 1]) == 5          # only 5 at idx 0 qualifies
    assert solution([3, 13, 2, 9]) == 3         # only 3 at idx 0 qualifies
    assert solution([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 4          # 1 (idx 0) + 3 (idx 2)
    assert solution([1, 1, 1, 1, 1]) == 3       # 1 + 1 + 1 at idx 0, 2, 4

    # Edge cases
    assert solution([]) == 0                    # empty list
    assert solution([7]) == 7                   # single odd element at idx 0
    assert solution([4]) == 0                   # single even element
    assert solution([2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) == 0    # even values at even indices
    assert solution([2, 1, 4, 3]) == 0          # odd values only at odd indices

    # Negative numbers (Python: -3 % 2 == 1, so negative odds qualify)
    assert solution([-3, 2, -5, 4]) == -8       # -3 (idx 0) + -5 (idx 2)
    assert solution([-2, -1, -4, -3]) == 0      # even values at even indices

    # Larger mixed case
    assert solution([1, 0, 1, 0, 9, 0, 7]) == 17  # 1 + 1 + 9 + 7
